 Journalists denied access to Steve Smith’s NSW training amid ball-tampering claims 
 By
 TNM (With ANI Inputs) 
 ✓
 20 November 2026, 10:10 am 
 3 min read
 20 Nov 2026 
 ANI Photo | Journalists denied access to Steve Smith’s NSW training amid ball-tampering claims 
 Journalists and cameras were refused access to a New South Wales training session involving Steve Smith on Friday amid renewed controversy over the 2018 ball-tampering scandal following revelations from Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft.
 Smith, who returned to training at the Sydney Cricket Ground (SCG) after a limited tour of South Africa due to injury and poor form, was reportedly barred from media viewing, with cameras forced to film the session through a side gate, distant from where Smith was practising.

 Smith, who had been in New York since the South Africa tour ended, reportedly entered through a back entrance. Khawaja and Bancroft’s recent claims alleging wider team knowledge of ball tampering during the 2018 South Africa tour have reignited debate, with Smith—the then-captain who was banned for 12 months—remaining silent on the issue.
 Other players including David Warner, Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Mitchell Marsh have publicly commented. Warner supports Khawaja and Bancroft’s claims, while Cummins dismissed suggestions that bowlers were involved, calling such assertions “utter nonsense” during a recent press conference.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 New South Wales are preparing for their Sheffield Shield match against Queensland on Saturday, where Smith is not expected to participate. Cricket Australia, Cricket NSW and Smith’s management reportedly agreed to allow Smith some space as the cricket community awaits his response.
 The controversy resurfaced with Khawaja’s autobiography Sabr , which called for collective team responsibility and claimed that ball tampering was widely known within the squad, not limited to Smith, Warner and Bancroft. Khawaja alleged that sandpaper was used in a Test prior at Gqeberha and that the ball’s condition was manipulated during the 2017/18 Ashes series to achieve reverse swing.
 Following Cummins’ rejection of Khawaja’s claims, Bancroft authored a detailed 4,497-word column in The West Australian, corroborating Khawaja’s account. Bancroft described conversations with pace bowlers about reverse swing and claimed that sandpaper use was encouraged and celebrated by teammates and coaching staff, except for the team’s media manager Kate Hutchison.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Pat Cummins’ agent Neil Maxwell reiterated the captain’s consistent stance on the scandal, stating, “Pat’s position hasn’t changed in eight years. He has been consistent and adamant from day one. Pat feels for Cam, of course. He has been through a lot.” Maxwell added that Cummins has rebuilt the Australian team following the scandal.
 Meanwhile, Cricket Australia announced the creation of an “independent forum” to hear testimonies from players involved in the 2018 South Africa tour. CA chief executive Todd Greenberg clarified that this initiative will not reopen or re-prosecute the original investigation and that no new sanctions will be imposed. The board will decide which information to release upon the completion of the process, expected to take about a month.
